read_conclusion: the gap lives in the per-object transform and appearance reads. Removing the reads returns the arm to the pre-PD level; removing the wrapper, the validation or the call boundary does not. The remaining direction is a data-layout change (a compact per-frame presentation row that extract scans instead of touching the registry per object), which touches the read contract and is owner-scoped.

direction_compact_rows.design: RuntimeSession refreshes a compact PresentationRow array in publishPresentation (once per published mutation); the materializer's extract scans that array instead of touching the registry per object, with a per-object fallback whenever the rows are absent or short.
direction_compact_rows.workload: CUEXIS_FOLLOW_COUNTS=1800 2000 2000; five alternating pairs against baseline-pd-probe.exe
direction_compact_rows.verdict: rejected: extract falls 18.1% but update rises 49.0%, so the whole frame costs 10.5% more (180.40 -> 199.46 us). The row array is an extra memory pass over data that the snapshot already has to read once; it moves cost rather than removing it.
